mc.q: Which of the following can effectively format a document in word processing software?
st: Setting the default font as the most frequently-used font type and font size
mc.exp: Default font and pre-set styles both control formatting. Auto-correction fixes spelling/typing, not format.

mc.q: Which of the following additions of numbers in 8-bit two's complement representation will result in an overflow error?
mc.exp: Overflow only happens when two numbers of the SAME sign give a result of the opposite sign. D: 1011 1010 = −70, 1100 0100 = −60, sum −130 < −128 → overflow (result 0111 1110 looks positive).

mc.q: The ASCII codes for the characters 'X' and 'Z' in hexadecimal are ________ and 5A respectively.
mc.exp: X is two letters before Z: 5A − 2 = 58.

mc.q: When creating a database table in database software, what should users usually set?
st: The data type of each field
mc.exp: You define field data types and a primary key. You do not normally fix a maximum number of records.

mc.q: Eva uses WAV format instead of MP3 format when recording music performance. What is/are the benefit(s) of this?
st: The file size of the audio file is larger.
mc.exp: WAV is uncompressed, so quality is better. A larger file is a drawback, not a benefit. MP3 is just as cross-platform.

mc.q: Tim uses the 'table of contents' feature in word processing software. When inserting a new chapter, ________.
o: Tim has to input a formula for calculating the page numbers
Tim has to input the chapter name in the table of contents
the page numbers can be updated accordingly
the new chapter will be inserted as the last chapter
mc.exp: An automatic TOC is generated from headings, so page numbers and entries update automatically.

mc.q: John adds verbal annotations to a presentation file. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
st: The file size of the presentation increases.
The number of slides in the presentation increases.
Videos cannot be embedded in slides with a verbal annotation.
mc.exp: Audio narration is stored in the file, so size goes up. Slide count doesn't change, and videos can still be embedded.

mc.q: Mary is a marketing manager and plans to send invitation letters to selected customers. She will extract data from a customer database. What information processes should she do?
mc.exp: Filter to select customers, then mail merge to make letters. What-if analysis is for spreadsheet modelling.

mc.q: What is the purpose of asking a user to enter a password twice in an online system? (Registration form: Username / Password / Re-enter the password)
mc.exp: Double entry checks the data was entered as intended = verification. Validation checks data is reasonable (range, type, format).

mc.q: Peter wants to add the content in X.jpg and Y.xlsx to Z.docx using object linking. Which of the following statements about Object Linking and Embedding (OLE) is correct?
o: OLE does not apply to the file format of X.
The file size of X should be smaller than that of Z before Peter's action.
The file size of Z will be larger than that of Y after Peter's action.
Changes to data in Y can affect the subsequent printout of Z.
mc.exp: Linking keeps a reference to the source file, so editing Y updates what Z shows/prints. Linking (not embedding) barely changes Z's size.

mc.q: What is/are the major advantage(s) of using a form for data entry in database software?
st: It shortens the execution time of SQL statements.
mc.exp: Forms give a friendly layout with controls/validation → fewer input errors. They don't speed up SQL or save storage.

mc.q: The basic concept of the 'Input-Process-Output' cycle: X feeds into Process from above, and Process exchanges data both ways with Y below. What are X and Y?
mc.exp: A program controls the processing; storage is read from and written to (two-way arrow).

mc.q: Eva uses a spreadsheet to store hundreds of records of online meetings (columns: Date, Participant, Meeting code, Time, IP, Type). She wants to create a pivot table to find the number of meetings that each participant has attended. In which of the following areas should 'Participant' be put?
mc.exp: Participant goes in ROWS (one row per person) and also in VALUES as Count of Participant to count meetings. Only 28% got this right.

mc.q: Which of the following can be the specifications of a scanner for scanning documents and photos?
mc.exp: Scanners can have Wi-Fi (802.11n), a colour depth and onboard RAM as a buffer. All three are valid.

mc.q: Which of the following requires a driver program?
mc.exp: A device driver lets the OS talk to a hardware device such as a new printer.

mc.q: David builds a computer system at home that his friends can log in to and on which they can play an online football game together. Which of the following modes of processing is/are involved?
mc.exp: Players interact online and the game responds immediately (real-time). No batch jobs.

mc.q: John has a desktop computer installed with a 500GB SSD and a 2TB hard disk drive. Why is an operating system installed in the SSD instead of the hard disk drive?
o: The operating system is not open source software.
The files of the operating system are frequently used.
The storage size required for the operating system is smaller than 500 GB.
Data files need to be stored in the hard disk.
mc.exp: OS files are accessed all the time, so put them on the faster SSD.

mc.q: Which of the following is a recent development in CPU?
o: Decreasing the number of processing units
mc.exp: Of the options, only a higher clock rate is a real trend (along with more cores and lower power).

mc.q: Peter wants to buy a computer for using multimedia learning software packages. Which of the following is the least important factor?
mc.exp: ROM only holds firmware (BIOS/UEFI); its size doesn't affect running software.

mc.q: What are the advantages of using an e-book reading device instead of a tablet computer to read e-books?
mc.exp: E-ink readers use little power and are light; tablets are more powerful.

mc.q: The instruction of the assembly language 'LOAD 1000' is executed in a CPU. Which of the following components decodes the instruction?
mc.exp: The Control Unit fetches and decodes instructions. ALU does arithmetic/logic.

mc.q: Which of the following is commonly used for connecting two LANs?
mc.exp: Routers forward packets between different networks.

mc.q: Which of the following is not a multimedia file format?
mc.exp: ZIP is a compressed archive format.

mc.q: A supermarket will provide an online platform for customers to buy food. Which of the following should be considered when designing the user interface?
mc.exp: All three affect usability for different customers.

mc.q: Mary can use her mobile phone in her office to control the appliances connecting to a Wi-Fi network at home. Which of the following are involved?
mc.exp: Office → Internet → home LAN → Wi-Fi access point → appliance. Only 35% got all three.

mc.q: Mr Li rents online file storage services for the staff working in his office, instead of setting up file servers. Why?
st: The bandwidth of the Internet connection for the office is not sufficient.
Additional technical staff is not needed in the office.
It gives flexibility when increasing the storage size.
mc.exp: Cloud storage needs no in-house IT staff and scales easily. Low bandwidth would be a reason AGAINST cloud.

mc.q: Which of the following about HTTP is/are correct?
st: It is used to transfer hypertext documents.
It is used to translate URLs into IP addresses.
It is used to store the browsing history.
mc.exp: DNS translates domain names to IP. The browser stores history.

mc.q: In a school playground, although a wired network has been installed, the school installs an Access Point connecting to the network. Why?
st: Students can use tablet computers for lessons.
The network can be used 24 hours a day.
The data transfer rate for the network connections is higher.
mc.exp: An AP lets wireless devices join. Wired is usually faster, and both work 24 hours.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
X ← 9
Y ← 2
Repeat
    Output the remainder of (X / Y)
    X ← the integral part of (X / Y)
Until X = 0
mc.exp: Remainders: 9→1, 4→0, 2→0, 1→1. Output 1001 (this is 9 in binary, printed in reverse, which happens to be a palindrome).

mc.q: After writing the source code of a program, which of the following should be done according to the problem-solving procedures?
st: Outline the input and output requirements of the problem.
Test the program with boundary cases.
Define the scope of the problem.
mc.exp: (1) and (3) belong to problem definition/analysis, BEFORE coding. Testing comes after.

mc.q: Assume that X = 5, Y = 6 and Z = 7. Which of the following Boolean expressions returns TRUE?
mc.exp: Z > 10 is FALSE, so any '... AND (Z>10)' is FALSE. D: FALSE OR TRUE OR FALSE = TRUE.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm with the initial values in the array P?
P[1]=0, P[2]=1, P[3]=1, P[4]=0

Q ← 0
for i from 1 to 4 do
    If P[i] = 1 then
        Q ← 1 − Q
    Output Q

What is the output of the following algorithm?
sum ← 0
j ← 12
Repeat
    sum ← sum + 1
    j ← j − 2
Until j <= 2
Output sum
mc.exp: j: 12→10→8→6→4→2, the loop runs 5 times. Repeat-until checks AFTER the body.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
For i from 1 to 5 do
        A[i] ← i
S ← 0
i ← 1
While i > S do
        S ← S + A[i]*A[i+1]
        i ← i + 1
Output S
mc.exp: i=1 > S=0, so S = 0 + 1×2 = 2 and i = 2. Now i > S is 2 > 2, false, so the loop stops. Output 2.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
X ← 6
Y ← 4
H ← 2
While H > 0 do
        X ← X + Y
        Y ← X - Y
        X ← X - Y
        H ← H - 1
Output Y
mc.exp: The three lines swap X and Y. Swapping twice puts them back: Y = 4.

mc.q: What can Alice do when using open source software?
st: Seek approval from the software developer before using the software.
Amend the source code for her own use.
Amend the source code drastically and own the copyright of the entire software.
mc.exp: Open source lets anyone use and modify the code without asking, but she cannot claim copyright of the whole software.

mc.q: What should be considered when using information from the Internet to write a report?
st: Some information on the Internet is unreliable.
Most information on the Internet is free.
Many hackers steal personal information through social media.
mc.exp: Reliability of the source matters for a report. Price and hacking are not about using the information.

mc.q: Which of the following can narrow the digital divide in the society?
st: Providing computers to students for learning
Providing self-service kiosks for ordering food in restaurants
Using electronic payment to replace cash payment in shops
mc.exp: Giving people access to computers narrows the gap. Kiosks and e-payment push people without IT skills further out.

mc.q: Which of the following Internet activities are probably infringements of copyright?
st: Extracting a video from an old movie DVD and uploading it to the Internet
Drawing a picture and sharing it with friends using peer-to-peer (p2p) software
Downloading newspaper articles from the Internet and publishing a book containing them
mc.exp: (1) and (3) reuse other people's work without permission. Sharing your own drawing is fine, even over p2p.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the common measures for online systems to authenticate user identities?
mc.exp: Security tokens prove who the user is. DNS resolves names and firewalls filter traffic; neither authenticates users.

lq.stem:
Mrs Wong builds a wireless network at home such that her son, John, can use a tablet computer to access the Internet. The network is shown below:
[Diagram: Tablet computer ))) wireless to Z; Z wired to X; X wired to Internet; Z wireless to Mrs Wong's desktop computer; Printer wired to Mrs Wong's desktop computer]

parts.q: X and Z are network devices. The tablet computer is connected to Z for Internet access. What are X and Z?
parts.ms:
X: modem / router (1)
Z: Access Point / AP / wireless router (1)

parts.q: Refer to the above diagram, give two uses of the network for John, other than Internet access.
parts.ms:
Share printer / storage space → hardware sharing (1)
Exchange data (file sharing) → file sharing (1)

parts.q: Mrs Wong uses her desktop computer for more than 6 hours a day. State the health hazard due to the use of a mouse.
parts.ms: Repetitive use of wrist / finger / muscle / tendons of arm for data entry (1)

parts.q: Suggest a product for reducing this health hazard.
parts.ms: wrist rest / mouse with the ergonomic design (1)

parts.q: John uses his tablet computer 4 hours a day. Give two good practices for John to reduce the health hazard of this.
parts.ms:
Any two, 1 mark each:
Take short breaks periodically during the use. / Maintain a good posture. / Use an anti-glare screen cover. / Turn on the night shift mode to filter blue light. / Look at distant objects. / Use an ergonomic keyboard / mouse.
(simply 'look at green objects' ✗, unless the answer includes distant objects like trees)

parts.q: Mrs Wong buys food on a supermarket's web site. The web site uses a firewall and SSL technology to secure the online service. How can the firewall support a secured online service?
parts.ms: It can filter network traffic/block unauthorised access (1) to the server. (1)

parts.q: How can the SSL technology support a secured online service?
parts.ms: SSL encrypts information/sensitive data such as usernames and passwords, and credit card information (1) transmitted between Mrs Wong (customers) and the web site. (1)

lq.stem: A school library has a wireless network.

parts.q: Give two benefits of using a wireless network instead of a wired network in the library.
parts.ms:
Any two, 1 mark each:
Users can access network services anywhere in the library without the limitation of cable connection.
The number of network connections can be flexible.
Allows WiFi-only devices to access network services

The school buys two types of tablet computers, P and Q, with the following specifications for students to use:

CPU5 GHz, 10 cores1 GHz, 4 cores

Describe two differences in characteristics between RAM and SSD.
parts.ms:
Any two differences, 1 mark each:
RAM: volatile; higher data transfer rate; smaller storage size; CPU is able to access directly; holds program/data currently being executed by the CPU
SSD: non-volatile; lower data transfer rate; larger storage size; CPU is not able to access directly; holds program/data for long-term storage

parts.q: The CPU specifications of P are 5 GHz and 10 cores. Describe what they represent respectively.
parts.ms:
5 GHz: the clock rate of CPU (1)
10 cores: 10 processing units within a CPU (1)

parts.q: Without additional devices, suggest two ways that users input text in Q.
parts.ms:
Any two, 1 mark each: Virtual keyboard, speech recognition, handwriting recognition
Alternatives: on-screen keyboard, voice recognition, speech-to-text

parts.q: Students choose Q instead of P to conduct a survey on the street. Give two reasons to support their choice.
parts.ms:
allow Internet access via SIM card when WiFi is not available (1)
lighter in weight to increase portability (1)
✓ cellular network/mobile data (as an alternative to via SIM card)
✓ smaller in size (as an alternative to lighter in weight)
✗ lower power consumption

parts.q: School file servers, P and Q are installed with different operating systems, but files can be transferred between the devices through the network. Why?
parts.ms:
When the operating systems of all the devices use the same communication protocol for data communication, files can be transferred successfully. (2)
✓ FTP (as a specific example of the same communication protocol)
✓ TCP/IP (as a specific example of same communication protocol)

lq.stem:
Peter designs an algorithm to encrypt an array of binary digits, A, as shown below: 
I ← 5
repeat
        I ← I - 1
        A[I] ← 1 - A[I]
until A[I] = 1

parts.q:
Suppose that the initial content of A is:
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]
0011
What is the content of A after executing the algorithm?
parts.ms:
0 1 0 0 (1, 1)
Suggested answer: I=4: A[4]=0 (not 1, continue); I=3: A[3]=0; I=2: A[2]=1, stop. Result 0 1 0 0.

parts.q:
Suppose that the content of A after executing the algorithm is:
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]
1010
What is the initial content of A?
parts.ms:
1 0 0 1 (1, 1)
Suggested answer: the loop stops at the first flip that gives 1, so A[4] must have been 1 (→0) and A[3] 0 (→1, stop). A[1], A[2] unchanged: 1 0 0 1.

parts.q:
The algorithm cannot terminate properly if all entries in the initial contents of A are 1. Revise the algorithm such that it can terminate properly. 
I ← 5
repeat
        I ← I - 1
        A[I] ← 1 - A[I]
until (A[I] = 1) [____] [__________]
parts.ms:
OR (1)   (I = 1) (1)
i.e. until (A[I] = 1) OR (I = 1)

parts.q:
Peter rewrites the algorithm in (a)(iii) as an alternative algorithm. Complete the algorithm below. 
Flag ← 1
for I from [____] down to 1 do
    if Flag = [____] then
          A[I] ← 1 - A[I]
    if A[I] = [____] then
          Flag ← 0
parts.ms: 4 / 1 / 1 (1 mark each)

parts.q: Peter plans to post computer learning materials on a web site for the community to learn by themselves. Give two limitations of this e-learning activity in society.
parts.ms:
1 mark each:
People may not easily access the Internet. (Internet access/hardware)
People may find difficult in operating electronic devices to learn the online materials. (Digital divide/literacy)

lq.stem:
Ms Li has the following designs for searching for examination marks of students on a web page.
Design 1: Mark >= [Text box] Subject: [Chinese ▼ drop-down list] [OK] [Cancel]
Design 2: Mark >= [0 ▼ list: 0, 10, 20, 30] Subject: ☐ Chinese ☒ English ☐ Math (check boxes) [OK] [Cancel]

parts.q: Which design is better? Give two reasons to support your answer.
parts.ms:
Any two reasons for the chosen design, 1 mark each:
Design 1: Marks other than multiples of 10 can be entered. / One subject must be selected. / Avoid multiple subject selection. / The subjects to be chosen could be added easily without changing the layout. (Occupy less space)
Design 2: It ensures that numeric data is entered in the Mark. / One or more subjects can be entered. / All options can be viewed at a glance.

lq.stem:
A display consists of 15 × 15 pixels (rows 1–15, columns 1–15), as shown below:
[15 × 15 grid]
Each pixel displays a colour represented by a 2-bit code, as shown below:
ColourShort form2-bit code
RedR00
GreenG01
BlueB10
YellowY11

parts.q: How many bits are required for representing the pixels on the display? Show your calculation.
parts.ms:
15 × 15 × 2 = 450 bits (2)
- only expression: 1 mark
- only answer: 2 marks

parts.q:
A computer applies an encoding scheme that each row on the display is represented by one or more bit patterns. Each bit pattern consists of 6 bits. The first 2 bits represent a colour, and the remaining 4 bits represent the number of consecutive pixels (in binary notation) of the colour.
For example, the bit pattern 110100 represents 4 consecutive yellow pixels: 11 (Y) 0100 (4)
Write down the pixels that the bit pattern 100001 represents.
Colour: ______ Number of pixels: ______
parts.ms: Colour: Blue/B (1)  Number of pixels: 1 (1)

parts.q:
For example, the two bit patterns 110100 and 001011 represent a row of 15 pixels:
YYYYRRRRRRRRRRR
Write down the pixels represented by the following three bit patterns.
010100 100001 111010
parts.ms:
G G G G B Y Y Y Y Y Y Y Y Y Y (2)
Any one code correct: 1 mark

parts.q:
Write down the bit patterns for representing the following pixels in a row.
BBYBBBBBBBBBBBB
parts.ms:
100010   110001   101100 (2)
Any one correct: 1 mark

parts.q:
With the encoding scheme, how many bits are required for representing a row of 15 pixels in each of the following cases?
(1) All pixels are red.
(2) No two adjacent pixels are of the same colour.
parts.ms:
15 × 6 = 90 (2)
- only expression: 1 mark
- only answer: 2 marks

parts.q: What computer resource should be considered for implementing the encoding scheme, other than the storage size? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: The computation power (CPU) (1) should be considered because the encoding scheme involves extra computation for representation. (1)
